mainTopic: Going out on שבת with a slave's seal or bell: who made it, metal versus clay, neck versus clothing, and the rules for an animal
overview: This amud opens with the last line of an earlier discussion: an איסטמא is not included in the decree against עטרות כלות. רבי אבהו had said the כבול in the משנה is a woolen cap, and שמואל now says it is a slave's seal. The גמרא asks how this fits with שמואל's own ruling that a slave may go out with a seal on his neck. It answers that a seal the master made is allowed, and one the slave made for himself is forbidden. A seal on the clothing is forbidden even when the master made it, because if it breaks the frightened slave might fold the cloak and carry it on his shoulders. The גמרא supports this with רבי יוחנן's ruling and with שמואל's instruction to the רבנן of the ריש גלותא's house. Next, a ברייתא that forbids even the neck seal is resolved: a metal seal, which the master cares about, is forbidden, and a clay seal is allowed. The proof comes from the laws of טומאה. The גמרא then explains that the permitted bell on a slave's clothes is woven in, following רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע. Finally, it starts to question whether an animal's bell can become טמא, and that discussion continues on the next amud.

steps.title: An איסטמא Is Not Covered by the עטרות כלות Decree
steps.stepSummary: This is the closing line of the earlier discussion. An איסטמא is not forbidden under the decree against עטרות כלות.
steps.simpleTranslation: The decree against bridal crowns does not apply to it (the איסטמא).
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes its earlier discussion about the איסטמא, a woman's head ornament. It says that this ornament is not included in the rabbinic ban on bridal crowns.
steps.deeperAnalysis: After the חורבן, the רבנן banned bridal crowns as a sign of mourning. One might have thought every fancy head ornament was included. This line says the איסטמא is a different kind of ornament, so the ban does not cover it.

keyTerms.meaning: Bridal crowns, which were banned after the destruction of the בית המקדש
It does not fall under the rule of
A woman's head ornament, the subject of the earlier discussion

steps.confusionAlert: This line belongs to the previous topic. It is not part of שמואל's statement that comes next. The topic changes with the very next word, וּשְׁמוּאֵל.

phrases.english: It does not fall under the decree of bridal crowns.
phrases.notes: 'It' refers to the איסטמא from the earlier discussion.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the earlier discussion of the איסטמא, which began on the previous amud.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: An איסטמא is not included in the decree against bridal crowns.

steps.title: שמואל Explains the כבול as a Slave's Seal
steps.stepSummary: שמואל gives a different definition of the כבול in the משנה: it is the seal a slave wears.
steps.simpleTranslation: And שמואל said: The כבול we learned about in the משנה is a slave's seal.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings שמואל's explanation of the word כבול. According to him, it is the seal a slave wears to show who his master is, not a woolen cap.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אבהו had said the כבול is a woolen cap. שמואל disagrees and says it is a slave's identifying seal. Under שמואל's reading, the משנה is ruling that a slave may not go out on שבת with this seal.

keyTerms.meaning: A slave's seal or tag showing who owns him
The item in the משנה that may not be worn out on שבת

phrases.english: And Shmuel said:
It is a slave's seal that we learned about (in the mishna).
phrases.notes: This explains the word כבול in the משנה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic. It offers a second definition of כבול, alongside רבי אבהו's earlier one.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The כבול in the משנה, which may not be worn out on שבת, is a slave's seal.

steps.title: שמואל Seems to Contradict Himself
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא points out that שמואל elsewhere allows a slave to go out with a seal on his neck. That seems to clash with his reading of the משנה, which forbids the seal.
steps.simpleTranslation: Did שמואל really say this? But שמואל said: A slave may go out with a seal on his neck, but not with a seal on his clothing!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges שמואל using another ruling of his own. In that ruling, he allows a slave to go out on שבת wearing a seal on his neck.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 2, שמואל read the משנה as forbidding a slave's seal. Here he allows a seal on the neck. Both cannot be true unless something tells the two cases apart.

keyTerms.meaning: Did he really say this? (introduces a contradiction)
On his neck / on his clothing

phrases.english: And did Shmuel say this?
But didn't Shmuel say:
A slave may go out with a seal that is on his neck,
but not with a seal that is on his clothing!

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמִי אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל הָכִי? וְהָאָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks step 2 by setting it against another ruling of שמואל.
steps.kashyaTarget: שמואל's statement that the forbidden כבול is a slave's seal
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If שמואל allows a slave to wear a seal on his neck, he cannot also read the משנה as forbidding a slave's seal.

steps.title: A Seal Made by the Master Versus One Made by the Slave
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא resolves the contradiction. When the master made the seal, it is allowed. When the slave made it for himself, it is forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is not difficult. This ruling (allowed) is where his master made the seal for him. That ruling (the משנה, forbidden) is where the slave made it for himself.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that שמואל's two statements deal with two different situations. Who made the seal decides whether it is allowed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A slave will not dare remove a seal his master put on him, so there is no worry that he will take it off and carry it. A seal the slave made himself is up to him. He might take it off and carry it in the public domain, so the משנה forbids it.

keyTerms.meaning: It is not difficult (introduces an answer)
This case ... that case (splits two rulings into separate situations)

steps.confusionAlert: Keep the matching straight. The 'master made it' case goes with שמואל's ruling that the slave may go out. The 'made it himself' case goes with the משנה's ban on the כבול.

phrases.english: It is not difficult:
This is where his master made it for him,
phrases.notes: This is שמואל's ruling that the slave may go out with the seal.

phrases.english: that is where he made it for himself.
phrases.notes: This is the משנה's ban on the כבול.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction raised in step 3.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases (אוקימתא): each statement refers to a different kind of seal.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Both statements seemed to be about the same slave's seal, so they seemed to contradict.
steps.terutzMaskana: A seal made by the master is allowed because the slave will not remove it. A seal the slave made himself is forbidden because he might remove it and carry it.

steps.title: Then Why Not a Seal on the Clothing?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the answer. If שמואל's ruling is about a seal the master made, a seal on the clothing should also be allowed.
steps.simpleTranslation: In what case did you explain שמואל's ruling? Where his master made the seal for him. If so, why may he not go out with a seal on his clothing?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the answer from step 4. It points to the second half of שמואל's own ruling, which forbids a seal on the clothing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 4 said a seal the master made is safe because the slave will not remove it. That reasoning should apply whether the seal is on his neck or on his clothes. So why does שמואל forbid the seal on the clothing? The next step answers this.

keyTerms.meaning: In what case did you set (explain) it?

phrases.english: In what case did you establish this ruling of Shmuel —
where his master made it for him?
Then with a seal on his clothing, why not!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer given in step 4.
steps.kashyaTarget: The answer that שמואל's ruling refers to a seal the master made
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the reason is that the slave fears removing a seal his master made, that reason covers a seal on the clothing too. Yet שמואל forbids the seal on the clothing.

steps.title: The worry that a broken seal leads to carrying the cloak
steps.stepSummary: A seal on clothing is forbidden even when the master made it. The seal might break, and the frightened slave would fold the cloak and put it on his shoulders.
steps.simpleTranslation: Perhaps the seal will break. The slave will get scared, fold his cloak, and put it on his shoulder.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from step 5: why is a seal on the clothing forbidden even when the master made it?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The problem with a seal on clothing is not the seal itself. If it breaks, the slave may fear his master will see a cloak without a seal. He might then fold the cloak and carry it on his shoulder to hide it, and that counts as carrying in public on שבת. A seal on the neck does not lead to this kind of hiding, so it stays permitted.

keyTerms.meaning: Perhaps; introduces a worry about what might happen
It will break or snap off

steps.confusionAlert: Wearing the seal is not itself considered carrying. The problem is the chain of events it could lead to, which ends with the cloak being carried folded on the shoulder.

phrases.english: Perhaps it (the seal) will break,
and he will be afraid and fold it (the cloak)
phrases.notes: He fears his master will see the cloak without its seal.

phrases.english: and place it on his shoulder.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 5
steps.terutzResolutionType: A separate reason (a protective decree) explains the ban on the clothing seal
steps.terutzHavaAmina: If the master made the seal, it should be allowed anywhere, including on the clothing.
steps.terutzMaskana: A seal on clothing is forbidden for a different reason: the worry that it breaks and the slave carries the folded cloak.

steps.title: Carrying a folded cloak on the shoulders is real carrying
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן rules that someone who goes out on שבת with a folded cloak on his shoulders must bring a חטאת.
steps.simpleTranslation: This follows רב יצחק בר יוסף, who said in the name of רבי יוחנן: someone who goes out on שבת with a folded cloak resting on his shoulders must bring a קרבן חטאת.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a source showing that the worry in step 6 is serious. Carrying a folded cloak on the shoulder is a full Torah-level violation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A folded cloak on the shoulder is not being worn. It is being carried like a package. That is a real act of carrying, serious enough to require a קרבן חטאת. This explains why חכמים made a protective decree against the clothing seal.

keyTerms.meaning: Must bring a sin-offering (a Torah-level violation done by mistake)

steps.whyThisMatters: It sets the general rule that clothing counts as 'worn' only when worn in the normal way. Otherwise it counts as a carried load.

phrases.english: This is like the view of Rav Yitzchak bar Yosef,
for Rav Yitzchak bar Yosef said
that Rabbi Yochanan said:
One who goes out with a folded cloak
resting on his shoulders on Shabbat
must bring a sin-offering.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the answer of step 6 by showing the feared outcome is a full violation
steps.raayaObject: That carrying a folded cloak on the shoulder is a real violation, so the worry in step 6 justifies a decree
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי יוחנן's ruling, reported by רב יצחק בר יוסף

steps.title: שמואל's instruction to the רבנן of the ריש גלותא's house
steps.stepSummary: שמואל told the רבנן of the ריש גלותא's house not to go out with sealed cloaks. Only רב חיננא בר שילא was allowed, because the house was not strict with him.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is like what שמואל told רב חיננא בר שילא: all the רבנן of the ריש גלותא's house may not go out in sealed cloaks, except you, because the ריש גלותא's house is not strict with you.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a real-life case that uses the same worry about a seal on clothing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The רבנן of the ריש גלותא wore his seal on their cloaks, as servants of his house. If a seal broke, they might fear him and fold and carry the cloak, just like the slave. רב חיננא was not under that pressure, so the worry does not apply to him. This shows the decree depends on whether the person would actually be afraid.

keyTerms.meaning: The Exilarch, leader of the Jews in Bavel
Sealed cloaks, garments carrying an official seal

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows the reason behind the decree is fear of the authority. Where there is no fear, the decree is not applied.

phrases.english: And this is like what Shmuel said
to Rav Chinnana bar Sheila:
All the Sages of the Exilarch's house
may not go out in sealed cloaks,
except for you,
because they are not strict with you,
the people of the Exilarch's house.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִי הָא דַּאֲמַר לֵיהּ שְׁמוּאֵל לְרַב חִינָּנָא בַּר שֵׁילָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second support for the reasoning in step 6, this time from a practical ruling
steps.raayaObject: That a seal on clothing is forbidden out of fear that it breaks and the cloak gets carried
steps.raayaSupportSource: שמואל's instruction to רב חיננא בר שילא about the sealed cloaks of the ריש גלותא's house
steps.whatToRemember: A seal on the neck is allowed. A seal on clothing is forbidden, because a broken seal might lead a fearful wearer to carry the folded garment, and that is a real שבת violation.

steps.title: Returning to שמואל's ruling about the slave's seal
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא goes back to שמואל's ruling: a slave may go out with a seal on his neck, but not with a seal on his clothing.
steps.simpleTranslation: Back to the main point. שמואל said: a slave may go out with a seal on his neck, but not with a seal on his clothing.
steps.whatsHappening: The word גופא tells us the גמרא is returning to quote שמואל's ruling in full, so it can now discuss that ruling directly.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier, this ruling was only mentioned in passing. Now the גמרא quotes it fully: neck seal allowed, clothing seal forbidden. This sets up the support and the challenge that follow.

keyTerms.meaning: 'The matter itself': a return to a statement mentioned earlier in order to study it
A seal, a sign of ownership

phrases.english: The matter itself: Shmuel said:
A slave may go out with a seal on his neck
but not with a seal on his clothing.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to the ruling of שמואל that was quoted in step 3, now as its own topic
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A slave may go out on שבת with a seal on his neck, but not with a seal on his clothing.

steps.title: A ברייתא agrees with שמואל
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches exactly what שמואל said.
steps.simpleTranslation: A ברייתא also teaches this: a slave may go out with a seal on his neck, but not with a seal on his clothing.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows that שמואל's ruling matches a teaching from the time of the תנאים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words תניא נמי הכי mean 'it was also taught this way.' The ברייתא has the same wording as שמואל, so his ruling has earlier support.

keyTerms.meaning: 'It was also taught so': a ברייתא that supports what was just said

phrases.english: It was also taught this way in a baraita:
A slave may go out with a seal on his neck
but not with a seal on his clothing.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the ruling restated in step 9
steps.raayaObject: שמואל's ruling: neck seal allowed, clothing seal forbidden

steps.title: A second ברייתא forbids even the neck seal
steps.stepSummary: Another ברייתא says a slave may not go out with a seal on his neck or on his clothing. It also gives rules about a bell and about טומאה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Here is a contradiction. A slave may not go out with a seal on his neck, nor with a seal on his clothing, and neither of these can become impure. He may not go out with a bell on his neck, but he may go out with a bell on his clothing, and both of these can become impure.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא sets one ברייתא against the other. The new ברייתא forbids the neck seal, while שמואל and the first ברייתא allow it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first ברייתא allows the neck seal, but this ברייתא forbids it. So the two sources clash on exactly the point where שמואל was supported. The ברייתא adds side notes: the seals cannot become טמא, and the bells can. Within this ברייתא, both seals are forbidden, but the bell is split: forbidden on the neck and allowed on the clothing. That split is the reverse of שמואל's seal rule.

keyTerms.meaning: 'And they raised a contradiction': setting two sources against each other
This and that, both of them

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two pairs. The seals cannot become impure, while the bells can. And the bell rule runs the other way: forbidden on the neck, allowed on the clothing.

phrases.english: And they raised a contradiction:
A slave may not go out with a seal on his neck
nor with a seal on his clothing,
and neither of these can become impure.
And not with a bell on his neck,
but he may go out with a bell on his clothing,
and both of these can become impure.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the ruling and the supporting ברייתא from steps 9 and 10
steps.kashyaTarget: שמואל's ruling, and the ברייתא in step 10, that a slave may go out with a seal on his neck
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A second ברייתא explicitly forbids the neck seal, which directly contradicts the first ברייתא and שמואל.

steps.title: End of the challenging ברייתא: rules for an animal and for טומאה
steps.stepSummary: The second ברייתא continues: an animal may not go out with a seal or a bell, on its neck or on its covering, and neither item can become טמא. This completes the challenge against שמואל.
steps.simpleTranslation: And an animal may not go out with a seal on its neck, or a seal on its covering, or a bell on its covering, or a bell on its neck. Neither this nor that can become טמא!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing the quote of the ברייתא it brought in Step 11 as a challenge. With this, the contradiction to שמואל is now fully on the table.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For an animal, a seal or bell counts as a burden, not as clothing or jewelry, so the animal may not go out with it. The ברייתא also adds that these items cannot become טמא. The key point for the challenge was already stated in Step 11: this ברייתא forbids a slave's seal even on his neck, while שמואל and the first ברייתא allowed it.

keyTerms.meaning: Covering or garment (here, the animal's blanket)

steps.confusionAlert: This is not a new challenge. It is the second half of the same ברייתא from Step 11. The contradiction is about the slave's seal on his neck.

phrases.english: And an animal may not go out
neither with a seal that is on its neck,
nor with a seal that is on its covering,
nor with a bell that is on its covering,
nor with a bell that is on its neck;
neither this nor that can become ritually impure!
phrases.notes: End of the ברייתא. The contradiction to שמואל now stands.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְלֹא תֵּצֵא בְּהֵמָה לֹא בְּחוֹתָם שֶׁבְּצַוָּארָהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the quotation of the challenging ברייתא begun in Step 11.
steps.kashyaTarget: שמואל's ruling and the supporting ברייתא (Steps 9-10) that permit a slave's seal on his neck.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A second ברייתא forbids a slave's seal even on his neck, which directly contradicts the first ברייתא.

steps.title: Proposed answer: who made the seal
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that the ברייתא which permits the seal is about a seal the master made. The ברייתא which forbids it is about a seal the slave made for himself.
steps.simpleTranslation: Shall we say that this ברייתא is about a seal his master made for him, and that ברייתא is about a seal he made for himself?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries a first way to resolve the contradiction. The word לימא ('shall we say') signals that this answer is tentative and may be rejected.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the master put the seal on him, the slave is afraid to take it off, so there is no worry that he will carry it. If he made it himself, he might take it off and carry it in the street, so it is forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: Shall we say? (a tentative suggestion that is often rejected)

phrases.english: Shall we say:
this baraita (which permits) is where his master made it for him,
that baraita (which forbids) is where he made it for himself.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a first resolution to the contradiction raised in Steps 11-12.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Split cases (אוקימתא): who made the seal.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The two ברייתות seem to argue about the very same case.
steps.terutzMaskana: Permitted when the master made it; forbidden when the slave made it himself.

steps.title: Rejecting the 'who made it' answer
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא says no: both ברייתות are about a seal the master made.
steps.simpleTranslation: No. Both this and that are about a seal his master made for him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the answer from Step 13. It is setting up a different way to split the two ברייתות in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both ברייתות are now about the same kind of seal, one the master put on the slave. So 'who made it' cannot be the difference. Something else about the seal must explain why one ברייתא permits it and the other forbids it.

keyTerms.meaning: This and that, meaning both cases

phrases.english: No,
both this and that are where his master made it for him.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא, אִידִי וְאִידִי דַּעֲבַד לֵיהּ רַבֵּיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proposed split in Step 13.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the 'who made the seal' split entirely.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Both ברייתות are about a seal made by the master, so this cannot be the distinction.

steps.title: New answer: a metal seal versus a clay seal
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא that forbids the seal is about a metal seal. The one that permits it is about a clay seal. This follows רב נחמן in the name of רבה בר אבוה: an item the master cares about may not be worn out, and an item he does not care about may.
steps.simpleTranslation: Here it is a seal of metal, and here it is a seal of clay. This follows what רב נחמן said in the name of רבה בר אבוה: an item that the master cares about, one may not go out with it. An item that he does not care about, one may go out with it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives its real answer. The difference between the two ברייתות is what the seal is made of.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A metal seal is valuable, so the master cares about it. If it falls off, the slave will be afraid of his master and carry it home, which is forbidden on שבת. A clay seal is worth nothing, so if it falls the slave will just leave it, and there is no worry about carrying.

keyTerms.meaning: Cares about it, is strict about it
One may go out with it (on שבת)

steps.whatToRemember: The final answer: a metal seal is forbidden because the master cares about it and the slave may carry it if it falls. A clay seal is permitted because no one cares about it. This matches the idea from Step 8, where the deciding factor was whether the ריש גלותא's house was strict.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up which is which. Metal is forbidden and clay is permitted, because what matters is whether the master cares, not how sturdy the item is.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets out a general rule for going out on שבת: if the owner cares about an item, we worry that it will fall off and be carried.

phrases.english: and here (where it is forbidden), it is a seal of metal,
and here (where it is permitted), it is a seal of clay;

phrases.aramaic: וְכִדְרַב נַחְמָן אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר אֲבוּהּ:
phrases.english: and this follows what Rav Nachman said in the name of Rabba bar Avuh:
an item that his master cares about —
one may not go out with it.

phrases.aramaic: דָּבָר שֶׁאֵין מַקְפִּיד עָלָיו — יוֹצְאִין בּוֹ.
phrases.english: An item that he does not care about — one may go out with it.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכָאן בְּשֶׁל מַתֶּכֶת, וְכָאן בְּשֶׁל טִיט
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the rejected split from Step 13 with a new one.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Split cases (אוקימתא): what the seal is made of, backed by an Amoraic principle.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Both ברייתות seem to be about the same seal, so they appear to contradict each other.
steps.terutzMaskana: Metal seal is forbidden (the master cares about it). Clay seal is permitted (no one cares).

steps.title: Support from the words 'neither can become טמא'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא says the metal reading also makes sense from the ברייתא's statement that 'neither this nor that can become טמא.' If the seals are metal, this teaches something new: these seals cannot become טמא, even though metal vessels normally can.
steps.simpleTranslation: So too, it makes sense, since the ברייתא teaches: 'neither this nor that can become טמא.' It works well if you say they are of metal: these items cannot become טמא, but their regular vessels of metal can.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a support for its new answer from the wording of the forbidding ברייתא itself. The argument is completed in Steps 17 and 18.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Metal vessels normally can become טמא. So if the ברייתא is about metal seals, its statement 'these cannot become טמא' teaches something new: these seals are different from regular metal vessels. The implied point, finished in Step 17, is that this wording would be less meaningful if the seal were clay.

keyTerms.meaning: So too it makes sense (introduces logical support)
From the fact that it teaches
It works well if you say

steps.confusionAlert: The proof is not finished here. 'אי אמרת בשלמא' sets up a contrast, and the 'but if you say clay' half comes in Step 17.

phrases.english: So too it is reasonable,
from the fact that it teaches:
'neither this nor that can become ritually impure.'
It works well if you say it is of metal:
it is these items that cannot become impure,
but their regular vessels (of metal) can become impure.
phrases.notes: The contrast with a clay seal continues next.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the metal-versus-clay answer of Step 15 using the wording about the slave's seals quoted in Step 11.
steps.raayaObject: The answer that the forbidding ברייתא is about a metal seal.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא's own words 'זה וזה אין מקבלין טומאה', which teach something new only if the seal is metal.

steps.title: The clay reading would create a false implication
steps.stepSummary: If the ברייתא were about clay seals, its words would wrongly imply that ordinary clay vessels can become טמא.
steps.simpleTranslation: But if you say the ברייתא is about clay seals, you would have to read it like this: only these seals cannot become טמא, but normal clay vessels can. Is that really true?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא continues its proof from Step 16. It now shows that the clay reading does not work.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When a ברייתא says that certain items 'cannot become טמא,' it suggests that this is surprising. That suggests other vessels of the same material can become טמא. If the seals were clay, the ברייתא would be hinting that clay vessels normally become טמא. The next step shows that this hint is false.

keyTerms.meaning: Their vessels, meaning regular vessels of the same material

phrases.english: But if you say
that we learned it about seals of clay
then only these seals cannot become impure
which implies that real vessels of that material can become impure?!
phrases.notes: The tone is surprised. The גמרא is about to show this implication is wrong.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אִי אָמְרַתְּ בְּשֶׁל טִיט תְּנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: This is the second half of the proof begun in Step 16. Step 16 showed the metal reading works. This step shows the clay reading fails.
steps.raayaObject: The forbidding ברייתא is about metal seals
steps.raayaSupportSource: The wording 'neither this nor that can become טמא' makes no sense if the seals are clay

steps.title: Vessels of earth never become impure
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that vessels of stone, dung, and earth never become טמא, not by Torah law and not by Rabbinic law.
steps.simpleTranslation: But a ברייתא teaches: vessels made of stone, of dung, or of earth cannot become טמא at all, not by Torah law and not by Rabbinic law.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to show that the implication in Step 17 is false. Even full vessels of earth never become טמא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If even real clay vessels cannot become טמא, there is nothing new in saying that clay seals cannot become טמא. The ברייתא would have no reason to say it. So the clay reading of the seal ברייתא falls apart.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up כְּלֵי אֲדָמָה with כְּלֵי חֶרֶס. כְּלֵי חֶרֶס are fired earthenware, and they can become טמא. כְּלֵי אֲדָמָה are unfired clay, and they cannot.

phrases.english: But it was taught in a baraita

phrases.aramaic: כְּלֵי אֲבָנִים כְּלֵי גְלָלִים וּכְלֵי אֲדָמָה
phrases.english: Vessels of stone, vessels of dung, and vessels of earth
cannot become impure
not by Torah law
and not by Rabbinic law.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: This step supplies the outside source that proves the implication in Step 17 is false.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא stating that vessels of earth never become טמא

steps.title: Conclusion: the seal is metal
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא concludes that the forbidding ברייתא is about metal seals.
steps.simpleTranslation: So learn from this that the ברייתא is about metal seals. Yes, learn from it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא wraps up the proof. The forbidding ברייתא is talking about a metal seal.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The clay reading has been ruled out, so only the metal reading remains. This confirms the answer from Step 15, which followed רב נחמן in the name of רבה בר אבוה. A metal seal is something the master cares about, so the slave may not go out with it. A clay seal is something the master does not care about, so the slave may go out with it.

keyTerms.meaning: Learn from it; this is proven

steps.whatToRemember: The seal the slave may not wear out is metal. Metal is valuable to the master, so the slave might take it off and carry it. The seal the slave may wear out is clay, which the master does not care about.

phrases.english: Rather, learn from it that it is about metal seals.
Indeed, learn from it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: This step closes the proof from Steps 16 to 18 and confirms the answer from Step 15.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The forbidding ברייתא is about metal seals. This settles the challenge against שמואל.

steps.title: Quoting the rule about the bell
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the slave ברייתא: a slave may not go out with a bell on his neck, but he may go out with a bell on his clothes.
steps.simpleTranslation: The ברייתא said: a slave may not go out with a bell on his neck, but he may go out with a bell on his clothes.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic. It quotes another line from the slave ברייתא to set up a question in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The phrase אָמַר מָר tells us that the גמרא is going back to a source it already quoted, so it can study one detail. The detail here is a difference between two places on the slave. A bell on his neck is forbidden, and a bell on his clothes is allowed.

keyTerms.meaning: 'The Master said.' The גמרא uses this to quote an earlier source again so it can discuss it.

phrases.english: The Master said:
and not with a bell on his neck,
but he may go out with a bell on his clothes.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: The seal discussion is finished. This step goes back to the slave ברייתא to look at its rule about bells.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A slave may not go out with a bell on his neck, but he may go out with a bell on his clothes.

steps.title: Why is a bell on clothes any different?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the rule. The worry that a bell might come off and be carried should apply to a bell on clothes too.
steps.simpleTranslation: Why is a bell on the neck forbidden? Because it might come off, and he would end up carrying it. Then we should worry that a bell on the clothes might also come off and be carried!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why the ברייתא treats the two bells differently. The same worry seems to apply to both.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The reason the neck bell is forbidden is the fear that it will come off and the slave will carry it in the public domain. A bell sewn or tied to clothing could also come off. So the line between neck and clothes seems to have no basis.

keyTerms.meaning: Perhaps it will come off or break off
And he will come to carry it

phrases.english: A bell on his neck, why not?
Because it might come off and he will carry it?
Then a bell on his clothes too,
let us worry that it might come off and he will carry it!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: This step challenges the rule just quoted in Step 20.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's difference between a bell on the neck and a bell on the clothes
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The reason given for the neck bell, that it may come off and be carried, applies just as much to a bell on clothing. So the two cases should have the same rule.

steps.title: The permitted bell is woven into the clothing
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the bell allowed on the slave's clothes is one woven into the fabric, so it cannot fall off.
steps.simpleTranslation: What case are we dealing with here? A case where the bell is woven into the garment.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge from Step 21. It explains that the bell allowed on the slave's clothes is woven right into the fabric.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The challenge was that a bell on clothes could also fall off, and then the slave might carry it. The answer narrows the case. A bell woven into the cloth is part of the garment, so it will not come loose and there is no risk of carrying.

keyTerms.meaning: With what case are we dealing here? (a formula that narrows a source to a specific case)
A skilled weaver (the bell was woven in by an expert)

phrases.english: With what are we dealing here?
Where a skilled weaver wove it into the garment.
phrases.notes: The bell is firmly woven into the fabric and is part of the garment.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of Step 21
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A bell on clothes could fall off just like a bell on the neck, so it should also be forbidden.
steps.terutzMaskana: The permitted bell is woven into the garment, so there is no fear that it will fall off.

steps.title: רב הונא's rule: woven items were never forbidden
steps.stepSummary: The answer fits the rule of רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע that חכמים made no גזירה against anything woven into a garment.
steps.simpleTranslation: This follows רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע, who said: anything that is woven in, the חכמים did not forbid.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא backs up its answer with a known rule from רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע. Anything woven into a garment was never included in the rabbinic prohibition.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This shows that Step 22 is not a forced answer. It rests on an existing general principle. Something woven in counts as part of the clothing itself, so the גזירה against carrying never applied to it.

keyTerms.meaning: They (the חכמים) did not make a decree
רב הונא, son of Rav Yehoshua, an אמורא

steps.whatToRemember: A slave's bell on his neck is forbidden. A bell woven into his clothing is permitted, because woven items are part of the garment and חכמים never forbade them.

phrases.english: And this follows Rav Huna, son of Rav Yehoshua.

phrases.aramaic: דְּאָמַר רַב הוּנָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב יְהוֹשֻׁעַ:
phrases.english: For Rav Huna, son of Rav Yehoshua, said:
Anything that is woven in, they did not decree against.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the answer of Step 22 with an established rule
steps.raayaObject: The claim that a woven bell is permitted
steps.raayaSupportSource: The statement of רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע: כל שהוא ארוג לא גזרו

steps.title: The animal ruling: no seals or bells, and they cannot become impure
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the ברייתא: an animal may not go out with a seal or a bell, on its neck or its clothing, and none of these can become טמא.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Master said: An animal may not go out with a seal on its neck, or a seal on its clothing, or a bell on its neck, or a bell on its clothing. Neither of these can become טמא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings back the ברייתא about animals so it can examine one of its claims. This sets up the challenge in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For animals, everything is forbidden, whether on the neck or on the clothing. This is unlike the slave, whose bell on his clothes was permitted. The ברייתא also adds that animal seals and bells cannot become טמא, and that detail is what the גמרא will question next.

keyTerms.meaning: The Master said (a formula that quotes a source already mentioned)

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two ברייתות. For a slave, a bell on his clothes is permitted. For an animal, a bell is forbidden even on its clothing.

phrases.english: The Master said: An animal may not go out
not with a seal that is on its neck,
nor with a seal that is on its clothing,
nor with a bell that is on its neck,
nor with a bell that is on its clothing;
this and that cannot become ritually impure.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the slave ברייתא to the animal ברייתא in order to analyze it
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An animal may not go out with a seal or a bell, on its neck or its clothing, and these items cannot become טמא.

steps.title: Another source says an animal's bell can become impure
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how an animal's bell could be unable to become טמא, since another ברייתא says it does become טמא.
steps.simpleTranslation: Can an animal's bell really not become טמא? They contrasted it with another source: an animal's bell is טמא...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא questions the last line of the animal ברייתא. It brings another ברייתא that says the opposite: an animal's bell can become טמא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first ברייתא said animal bells cannot become טמא. The new ברייתא says they can. The two sources seem to contradict each other, and the גמרא will need to explain the difference. This passage ends in the middle of the quoted source.

keyTerms.meaning: And they contrasted them (a formula that introduces a contradicting source)

phrases.english: And does an animal's bell not become ritually impure?
And they contrasted it with another source:
The bell of an animal is ritually impure (can become impure),
phrases.notes: The quote continues on the next amud.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְזוֹג דִּבְהֵמָה אֵין מְקַבְּלִין טוּמְאָה? וּרְמִינְהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the טומאה claim in the ברייתא quoted in Step 24
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's statement that an animal's bell cannot become טמא
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Contradiction between sources: another ברייתא explicitly says an animal's bell can become טמא.
